idea-plugin.name: Mobiscout
idea-plugin.description:
Mobiscout - Intelligent Mobile Testing Platform

Point the IDE at a running app and get the artifacts a tester needs — a per-screen element inventory, the app's interaction graph, and runnable tests — into a new or existing framework, without leaving the IDE. Local-first: the engine runs on your machine, no servers.

Key Features:

  • 📱 Device Management - Control Android emulators and iOS simulators directly from IDE
  • 🔍 UI Element Inspector - List the current screen's elements and copy or generate a ranked locator for any of them
  • 📊 Live Device Logs - Stream logcat/simctl logs in real-time
  • 🎯 Interactive Control - Tap the device screen from the IDE, mirrored live
  • 🧠 Ranked, self-healing selectors - accessibility-id → resource-id → text, with fallbacks; element types from a hybrid ML + heuristic classifier
  • 🔄 Interaction Graph - the app's navigation map, mined into multi-step, form-filling test paths, with structural findings (unreachable / dead-end screens)
  • 🌍 Multi-Language - generate tests in Python, Java, Kotlin and JavaScript, imperative or BDD, flat files or Page-Object structure
  • 🔌 Backends - Appium (Android UiAutomator2 + iOS XCUITest) and on-device Espresso
  • 🔐 Gates - pass login, TOTP/2FA, biometric, QR/document-scan and permission prompts to test behind them
  • ➕ Only what's new - generate tests only for what your existing suite doesn't already cover

Requirements:

  • For Android: Android Studio's SDK and an emulator or a connected device. Crawling over adb needs nothing more; Appium-mode crawls and running the generated kit need Node + Appium (npm i -g appium, then appium driver install uiautomator2).
  • For iOS (macOS): Xcode and a simulator, plus Node + Appium with the xcuitest driver (iOS crawls and kits run through Appium/XCUITest).

No separate engine to install — Mobiscout sets up its own local engine automatically on first use. Appium (above) is the one external tool the generated tests run against; the plugin tells you if it isn't reachable rather than failing silently.

Getting started:

  1. Open View → Tool Windows → Mobiscout.
  2. Connect a device or boot an emulator.
  3. Point it at your app and generate a test kit.

Docs at the repository; questions and bugs via GitHub Issues.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.12.3 — kits that compile, reachable gated screens, Windows-safe engine

  • Generated kits compile on real apps. A label containing a line break, or a screen titled like "2FA Setup", used to produce source that Java, Kotlin, JS, Python or Maestro rejected. Checked against the real toolchains — 11 failures before, none now. BDD kits, smoke kits and page objects were fixed the same way.
  • Everything behind a login is tested again: a gate reached mid-crawl left the whole post-auth app marked unreachable with no tests, and gated tests began typing credentials on the launch screen. Both fixed.
  • Windows: device names, paths and commands are read as UTF-8 end to end, so a non-ASCII profile folder or device name no longer breaks the engine connection.
  • Honest environment reporting: a stale Android SDK path, an emulator that failed to boot, and a missing or slow adb are each reported as what they are instead of passing silently or showing an empty device list.
  • Espresso, launch args and the Appium-server override now work in every target, not just Python; the security scanner's TLS check actually detects TLS 1.0/1.1 again; element classification and model training are reproducible, so the same crawl produces the same kit on every machine.

0.12.2 — project-wide review: safer crawls, sturdier engine, honest UI

  • Deeper crawls: the screen behind a mid-crawl gate (a login/OTP you tap into) is now explored, not mapped as one dead node; forms are cleared before typing so the invalid and valid passes are both real; a money field revealed by scrolling re-arms the "don't move money" gate.
  • Never taps the wrong button: a permission grant (and the blocking-dialog handler) no longer taps "Don't Allow"; onboarding auto-skip no longer treats a form's "Done" as a skip; a stale-coordinate tap after a failed back-out is prevented.
  • Sturdier engine: iOS swipe direction fixed; screenshots are platform-aware (a host without adb no longer crashes an iOS capture); a rejected Android tap is an error, not a fake success; the device log stream actually stops when you stop it.
  • Tool-window polish: the Generate dialog's collapsed "Advanced" no longer leaves a dead gap; the screen mirror scales to a short window; Live stops and warns once on failure instead of storming; actions report the real cause and never freeze the IDE.
  • Honest feature list and a packaging fix so iOS/Appium crawls no longer fail with "No package metadata was found for Appium-Python-Client".

0.12.1 — crawl-safety follow-ups

  • A transfer form whose amount field is identified only by its id (no visible currency symbol or hint word) is now recognised as a money screen, so its Send/Confirm is blocked by default — while OTP, phone-OTP and messaging screens stay crawlable.

0.12.0 — tool-window polish, safer crawls, hardened engine

  • Native tool window: the Devices/Screen/Logs/Inspector toolbars are now real IDE ActionToolbars; the Generate dialog groups the rarely-used knobs under a collapsible "Advanced", browses for the output folder, and validates before it runs.
  • Honest feedback: the generated kit lands in your project with an "Open folder" action; the progress bar shows the live crawl, not a frozen "Crawling…"; errors are non-modal balloons; the Logs view is bounded and no longer yanks you to the bottom while you read.
  • Live screen mirror: a "Live" toggle auto-refreshes while a session is active; the Inspector lets you copy a locator or generate a ranked, self-healing selector for the selected element.
  • Never freezes the IDE: every engine call (start, screenshot, …) runs off the UI thread, asserted at the service boundary so a regression fails loudly.
  • Safer crawls: a default crawl never taps money-moving controls (Pay/Buy/Transfer/… and Send/Confirm on a screen with a money field) — while OTP "Send code", messaging and email-confirmation flows are still crawled. Use --allow-destructive only on throwaway/sandbox apps.
  • Hardened Rust engine: the accelerated core is version-gated across the Python↔Rust seam, so a stale build degrades loudly instead of silently.

0.11.0 — Maestro, MCP, and crawl intelligence

  • New codegen target: Maestro declarative YAML flows (cross-platform, no Appium) — a 9th target alongside Python/Java/Kotlin/JS, imperative and BDD.
  • MCP server (mobiscout mcp): drive the engine from an AI agent (Claude, etc.) over the Model Context Protocol — list targets, generate tests from an IR, crawl an app. The engine stays deterministic and offline; no runtime LLM.
  • Coverage artifact: every kit now includes coverage.md + coverage.json — what the crawl reached vs what the generated kit tests (reachable / unreachable / gated / dead-end screens, element and screen coverage).
  • Diff-aware regeneration (crawl --diff / --only-changed): re-crawl an evolving app and get a CHANGES.md of added/changed/removed tests — regenerate only the delta, not the whole app.

0.10.0 — one path, zero setup

  • Generate now leads with "Detect from project…": point at your repo and it finds the app(s) — Android applicationId, iOS bundle id — and fills the form for you.
  • A project with more than one app (Android + iOS) can be generated in one action, crawled in parallel, each on its own device.
  • No device running? The flow boots one for you — an installed Android emulator or a shut-down iOS simulator — and waits for it, instead of returning an empty crawl. You're only asked when there's genuinely nothing to boot.
  • The device picker auto-matches a running device to the app's platform.
  • The old setup wizard is gone: the engine installs and starts itself in the background, so there's nothing to set up before the first run.

0.9.1

  • Android now works when the IDE is launched from Finder/Dock — the engine resolves the Android SDK onto PATH, so adb/emulator are found (Devices, Boot and crawls no longer silently see no Android device).
  • Generate Test Kit: the device is a dropdown of running devices (pick by name, no more hunting for a UDID); the form leads with the essentials and groups the rest under "Advanced".
  • Devices tab: shows running/connected devices first (no wall of idle simulators), with platform glyphs and colored status.
  • Errors and results now use notification balloons instead of modal pop-ups; a crawl that reaches 0 screens is reported honestly as a warning, not a success.

0.9.0 — public beta

  • First public beta. Point the IDE at a running app and get an element inventory, an interaction graph, and runnable tests, without leaving the IDE.
  • Runnable-project scaffolds for Java (Maven) and Kotlin (Gradle).
  • Anti-flake generated tests: a settle() wait after each transition.
  • Stream app logs and capture crashes into the kit.
  • Native tool-window toolbar and actionable empty states.
